 The Board of County Commissioners sit jointly as the following boards: Liquor Board, License Board,
 Tahoe-Douglas Transportation District Board, Water District Board, and the Redevelopment Agency.
 Agenda items may be taken out of order, may be combined for consideration, or may be removed from
 the agenda at any time. All items designated “for possible action” may include discussion by the
 County Commissioners and they may take action to approve, modify, deny, take “no action,” or
 continue the item.

 To Watch the Meeting : Members of the public may click on the following link to watch the
 livestream     of      the    Board      of    County        Commissioners       meeting:
 https://www.youtube.com/@douglascountynevada

 Written Public Comment : To offer public comment before the Board meeting, members of the public
 may submit public comments online through the County’s public comment form by clicking on the
 following link:
 https://www.douglascountynv.gov/government/board_of_county_commissioners/public_comment

 Public Comment During the Meeting : Members of the public may attend the meeting in person at the
 address listed at the top of the agenda to provide public comment.

 Supporting Materials:
 Copies of supporting material can be requested in person from the Douglas County Clerk/Treasurer's
 Office, 1616 8th Street, Minden, Nevada or by calling Nicki Oehlerking at 775-782-9014. Electronic
 copies of the agenda and supporting materials are also available at the following websites:

 State of Nevada Public Notices Website: https://notice.nv.gov/
 Douglas County Meeting website: https://douglascountynv.granicus.com/ViewPublisher.php?
 view_id=1

 Notice to Persons with Disabilities:
 Members of the public who are disabled or require special assistance or accommodations are requested
 to notify the Douglas County Manager's Office in writing at Post Office Box 218, Minden, Nevada
 89423 or by calling 775-782-9821 at least 20 hours in advance of the meeting.

 Members of the public may call the County Manager’s office at 775-782-9821 to obtain help
 making public comment using any of the foregoing methods.

 A copy of the finalized agenda is posted at the Minden Inn at 1594 Esmeralda Avenue, Minden
 Nevada.

Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                          November 5, 2026
                                                                                                     1

DOUGLAS COUNTY BOARD OF COUNTY COMMISSIONERS

                                           FINAL AGENDA

                                           November 5, 2026

 LUNCH BREAK
 The Board of County Commissioners may break for lunch at approximately noon and will
 reconvene after a break at the discretion of the Chairperson.

 1.   CALL TO ORDER

 2.   PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
      Led by Commissioner Sharla Hales

 3.   PUBLIC COMMENT (No Action)
      Forum Restrictions and Orderly Conduct of Business
      The Board of County Commissioners conducts the business of Douglas County and its citizens
      during its meetings. The Board may impose reasonable, content-neutral restrictions on public
      comment such as comments that are on topics that are not within the jurisdiction, authority, or
      control of the Board of County Commissioners, or if the content of the comment is willfully
      disruptive of the meeting by being irrelevant, repetitious, slanderous, offensive, inflammatory,
      irrational, or amounts to a personal attack or interfering with the rights of other speakers. The
      presiding officer may order the removal of any person whose statement or other conduct disrupts
      the orderly, efficient or safe conduct of the meeting. Warnings against disruptive comments or
      behavior may or may not be given prior to removal. Hand clapping, making remarks or gestures
      from the audience that may interrupt, interfere or prevent any speaker from commenting should
      not occur.

      Responses to Public Comments
      The Board of County Commissioners can deliberate or take action only if a matter has been listed
      on an agenda properly posted prior to the meeting. During the public comment period, speakers
      may address matters listed or not listed on the published agenda as long as those matters are within
      the jurisdiction and control of the Board of County Commissioners. The Open Meeting Law does
      not expressly prohibit responses to public comments by the Commissioners. However, responses
      from Commissioners to unlisted public comment topics could become deliberation on a matter
      without notice to the public. On the advice of legal counsel, and to ensure the public has notice of
      all matters the Board of County Commissioners will consider, Commissioners may choose not to
      respond to public comments, except to correct factual inaccuracies, ask clarifying questions, or to
      ask that a matter be listed on a future agenda.

      Public comment is limited to three minutes per speaker unless additional time is granted by the
      Board Chairperson. The Board of Commissioners uses timing lights to ensure that everyone has
      an opportunity to speak. You will see a green light when you begin, and then a yellow light which
      indicates that you have thirty seconds left and should conclude your comments. Once the light
      turns red, please sit down.

     In addition to opening public comment, public comment will also be taken on administrative
Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                   November 5, 2026
                                                                                                2

agenda items that are identified for possible action and closing public comment. If you plan to
      speak on a specific agenda item that is on the administrative agenda and identified for possible
      action, then please provide your public comment when that agenda item is heard. Public
      comment will not be taken on Liquor Board agenda items. If you would like to provide public
      comment on Liquor Board agenda items, please provide your public comment during opening
      public comment or closing public comment.

      Public comment must be limited to matters that are within the jurisdiction and control of the
      Board of County Commissioners. Public comment must be addressed to the Chairperson and not
      to members of the public so that the Board may take future action on the issues that are raised by
      the public.

      At this time, public comment will be taken on those items that are within the jurisdiction and
      control of the Board of County Commissioners.

 4.   APPROVAL OF AGENDA
      For possible action. Approval of the proposed agenda. The Board of Commissioners reserves the
      right to take items in a different order to accomplish business in the most efficient manner, to
      combine two or more agenda items for consideration, and to remove items from the agenda or
      delay discussion relating to items on the agenda.

 APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MINUTES

      5.   For possible action. Discussion to approve the minutes of the regular meeting on October 1,
           2026, of the Board of County Commissioners.

 6.   RECESS AS BOARD OF COUNTY COMMISSIONERS CONVENE AS DOUGLAS
      COUNTY LIQUOR BOARD

 DOUGLAS COUNTY LIQUOR BOARD

      7.   For possible action. Discussion to approve the addition of David Luciano Hochgurtel to the
           existing Unrestricted On-Site Retail Liquor License for The Corner Bar, LLC, dba The
           Corner Bar, represented by owner Pasquale Cioffi. David Luciano Hochgurtel has signed a
           Waiver of Notice of Hearing. The Corner Bar, LLC, dba The Corner Bar, is located at 1596
           Esmeralda Avenue, Minden, Nevada. (Captain Koontz)

 8.   ADJOURN AS DOUGLAS COUNTY LIQUOR BOARD RECONVENE AS BOARD OF
      COUNTY COMMISSIONERS

 CONSENT CALENDAR
 Items appearing on the Consent Calendar are items that can be adopted with one motion unless an item
 is pulled by a Commissioner or a member of the public. Members of the public who wish to have a
 consent item placed on the Administrative Agenda shall make that request during the public comment
 section at the beginning of the meeting and specifically state why they are making the request. If items
 are pulled for discussion by a vote of the Board of County Commissioners, they will automatically be
 placed on the Administrative Agenda to be heard at the discretion of the Chairperson or may be
 continued until another meeting.

 9.   CONSENT ITEMS
Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                           November 5, 2026
                                                                                                      3

A.   For possible action. Discussion on the Outdoor Festival License application submitted by the
          Town of Minden for Minden's Gazebo Lighting Celebration, to be held Friday, December 4,
          2026, from 3:00 PM to 9:00 PM, at Minden Park, 1606 Esmeralda Avenue, Minden, Nevada.
          (Amy Burgans, Clerk-Treasurer)

     B.   For possible action. Discussion on the Outdoor Festival License application submitted by
          Emily Lawrence, Marketing and Events Manager for Golden Nugget Lake Tahoe Hotel and
          Casino, for the New Year's Eve Party on the Plaza, to be held Thursday, December 31, 2026,
          to Friday, January 1, 2027, from 9:00 PM to 12:30 AM, at Golden Nugget Lake Tahoe Hotel
          and Casino, 50 Highway 50, Stateline, Nevada. (Amy Burgans, Clerk-Treasurer)

     C.   For possible action. Discussion on retroactively approving a one-year contract extension with
          Government Software Assurance Corporation (GSA), in the amount of $97,350, for the 2026-
          27 Property Tax Bill software, and authorize the Douglas County Clerk-Treasurer to sign any
          required documents. (Amy Burgans, Clerk-Treasurer)

     D.   For possible action. Discussion to approve the First Amendment to a Contract for
          Professional Services between RAD Strategies and Douglas County to increase the contract
          amount from $33,600 to $52,800 for content creation services for Douglas County with the
          addition of supporting the County during the vacancy of the Community Relations Manager
          position, as needed. (Kathy Lewis, Chief Operating Officer)

     F.   For possible action. Discussion to accept a $15,000 grant from the Carson Subconservancy
          District Noxious Weed Abatement Program, and authorize the Community Services Director
          to sign all related grant documents. (Brook Adie, Community Services Director)

     G.   For possible action. Discussion to accept the Public Administrator’s 2026 Third Quarter
          Report for the period beginning July 1, 2026, and ending September 30, 2026, per Douglas
          County Code Chapter 2.23. (Brook Adie, Community Services Director)

     H.   For possible action. Discussion to accept the Public Guardian’s 2026 Third Quarter Report
          for the period beginning July 1, 2026, and ending September 30, 2026, per Douglas County
          Code 2.22.135. (Brook Adie, Community Services Director)

     I.   For possible action. Discussion to renew the annual software subscription with NeoGov for
          various cloud-based modules for recruitment, development and management of employees,
          in an amount not to exceed $165,620, and authorize the Human Resources Director to sign
          any required documents. (Christine Vido, Human Resources Director)

     J.   For possible action. Discussion to accept the auditor's report on Douglas County's general
          ledger cash balances through September 30, 2026, per Nevada Revised Statute 251.030.
          (Kathy Kaiser, Comptroller)

     K.   For possible action. Discussion to approve a change order to increase the purchase order with
          Granite Construction Supply by $40,000, for a total purchase order of $85,000. (Nicole
          Hubbard, Administrative Services Manager)

     L.   For possible action. Discussion to approve the purchase of $96,278.75 in radio
          communication equipment from Kenwood KAIROS base stations/repeaters to replace all
          remaining Motorola Quantar and GTR repeaters in the County’s public safety radio system,
          and authorize the Chief Information Officer to sign all required documents. (Peace Ruggia,
Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                         November 5, 2026
                                                                                                    4

Chief Information Officer)

     M. For possible action. Discussion to accept the Grant of Permanent Easement and Agreement
        from Clear Creek Residential, LLC to Douglas County related to two water tanks and
        appurtenant infrastructure located within Parcel B6 of the Clear Creek Tahoe Unit 6 Final
        Map, and authorize the County Manager to sign any documents necessary to effectuate the
        easement. (Philip Ritger, Public Works Director)

     N.   For possible action. Discussion to approve the transfer of Real Property owned by Douglas
          County Nevada to the Nevada Department of Transportation and execute the Quit Claim
          deed. The Real Property to be transferred is described in the following recorded documents
          of Douglas County: Document Numbers 1970-47430, 1984-093937 and 1985-124073.
          (Philip Ritger, Director Public Works)

     O.   For possible action. Discussion regarding the adoption of Resolution 2026R-064, increasing
          the South Tahoe Refuse Company's trash disposal rates by the base year rate adjustment of
          9.42% for the 2027 calendar year, as allowed under the terms of the franchise agreement.
          (Philip Ritger, Public Works Director)

     P.   For possible action. Discussion to approve a $372,324.80 construction contract with Norberg
          General Engineering, LLC for the Advanced Water Metering Infrastructure Project, and
          authorize the Director of Public Works to execute the contract and change orders up to 10%
          of the original contract price. (Rick Robillard, Deputy Public Works Director)

     Q.   For possible action. Discussion to retroactively accept a $400,000 Public Safety Partnership
          and Community Policing Grants Grant from the Department of Justice (DOJ) Office of
          Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) for the time period of January 23, 2026,
          through January 31, 2028, for the purchase of one (1) Mobile Command Vehicle, and
          authorize the Chief Operating Officer to sign any required grant documents. (Undersheriff
          Elges)


     R.   For possible action. Discussion to approve a five-year contract between the Douglas County
          Sheriff's Office and Motorola Solutions, Inc. to provide Computer Aided Dispatch and
          related Records Management Services to the Douglas County Sheriff's Office and Douglas
          County Emergency Communications from July 1, 2027, through June 30, 2032, at a cost of
          $175,000 per year. (Undersheriff Elges)

     S.   For possible action. Discussion to authorize the Douglas County Sheriff’s Office to accept an
          unrestricted $10,000 donation from Scott and Susan McNealy, and adopt Resolution 2026R-
          058 to augment the budget for the donated funds. (Undersheriff Ron Elges)

     T.   For possible action. Discussion to accept the donation of a multi-purpose canine, valued at
          $25,000, from the Douglas County Sheriff's Advisory Council to the Douglas County
          Sheriff's Office. (Undersheriff Elges)

     U.   For possible action. Discussion to accept the Douglas County Sheriff's Office Quarterly Fee
          and Compensation Report for July 2026 through September 2026. (Undersheriff Elges)

 ADMINISTRATIVE AGENDA

Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                         November 5, 2026
                                                                                                    5

The Chairperson will read the agenda title into the public record and will have the discretion to
 determine how the item will be presented. Agenda items may be considered ahead of or after the
 schedule indicated by this agenda. Public comment will be taken on items that are identified for possible
 action.


 10. ITEM(S) PULLED FROM THE CONSENT AGENDA WILL BE HEARD AT THIS TIME

 PRESENTATIONS

      11.1 For presentation only. Ceremonial presentation of Proclamation 2026P-061 recognizing
           November 8-14, 2026, as Nevada Flood Awareness Week in Douglas County. (Courtney
           Walker, Stormwater Program Manager)

      11.2 For presentation only. Ceremonial presentation of Proclamation 2026P-062, recognizing the
           week of November 1-7, 2026, as National Animal Shelter Appreciation Week in Douglas
           County, Nevada. (Brook Adie, Community Services Director)

 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

      12. For possible action. Discussion on the adoption of Ordinance 2026-1675, amending Douglas
          County Code Title 18, Appendix B, the Minden Town Boundary, by annexing approximately
          6.68 acres into the Town of Minden boundary. The parcel to be annexed is Assessor's Parcel
          Number (APN) 1320-29-301-005. The parcel lies to the south of the intersection of Buckeye
          Road and Heybourne Road. It is owned by the Town of Minden. Second Reading. (Kate
          Moroles-O'Neil, Economic Vitality Manager and Interim Principal Planner)

 HUMAN RESOURCES

      13.1 For possible action. Discussion to approve the renewal of employee and retiree medical
           insurance and binding insurance coverage with Anthem for calendar year 2027 at a 19.5%
           premium increase for both the high deductible health plan (HDHP) and Preferred Provider
           Organization plan (PPO); and authorize the Human Resources Director to execute any
           required agreements and documents to bind coverage. (Christine Vido, Human Resources
           Director)

      13.2 For possible action. Discussion to renew Douglas County's vision insurance coverage with
           VSP Vision Care, with a 1.26% premium increase, for calendar years 2027 and 2028, and
           authorize the Human Resources Director to execute any related agreements and documents.
           (Christine Vido, Human Resources Director)

 COUNTY MANAGER

      14. For presentation only. Announcements, reports, and updates from County Commissioners
          and the County Manager, including information regarding boards or commissions on which
          they serve as members or liaisons, other meetings or functions attended, and Commissioner
          requests for discussion of potential future agenda items. Discussion may also include status
          reports and updates on County projects and administrative matters for the Board of County
          Commissioners. (Chairman Mark Gardner)


Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                            November 5, 2026
                                                                                                       6

15. CLOSING PUBLIC COMMENT (No Action)
     At this time, public comment will be taken on those items that are within the jurisdiction and
     control of the Board of Commissioners or those agenda items where public comment has not
     already been taken.

 16. ADJOURNMENT




Douglas County Board of County Commissioners                                      November 5, 2026
